items.title: 6 Ways to Wear the “Sense and Sensibility” Fashion Trend Without Looking Like a Costume
items.standfirst: Every few years, a period drama sends us all shopping for puffy sleeves. This time, the costumes are doing something different: they’re inspiring clothes we’d actually wear in…
body: Every few years, a period drama sends us all shopping for puffy sleeves. This time, the costumes are doing something different: they’re inspiring clothes we’d actually wear in our normal life.

Georgia Oakley’s new adaptation of “Sense and Sensibility,” in theaters now, skips the sugar-spun pastels of recent Regency romances . Her Dashwood sisters look like women who’ve been pushed out of their home and into the countryside. Costume designer Grace Snell leaned into that, and Daisy Edgar-Jones, who plays Elinor, told Bustle the director wanted a Dashwood family that’s “a little more undone, a little more of the earth.” The wardrobe is dyed with natural pigments (Snell has said Margaret’s berry-stained look is a favorite), the hair is looser than you’d expect , and the sisters share clothes. Snell has also pointed to ’90s tailoring as an influence on Elinor’s look.

The best part is that none of it requires a corset, a bonnet, or a trip to a costume shop. It’s all in the details: the colors, the silhouettes, the way a few pieces are layered and borrowed and worn a little undone. Here’s how to translate it into outfits you’d actually wear to brunch, the office, or a weekend errand run.

The film’s natural-dye palette is the easiest trend to wear. Skip the pastels and reach for deep berry, moss, rust, oat, and faded blue, in fabrics with some texture, like wool, linen, and brushed cotton. One colorful piece against neutrals is enough.
2. Try the Empire Waist, Without the Costume

The high waist is Regency fashion’s signature, and it’s easier to wear than it looks. Look for an empire-seam or babydoll dress in a heavier fabric, then ground it with boots and a chunky knit so it doesn’t read as a costume. A high-waisted midi skirt gets you the same silhouette with less commitment.

Here’s the secret: That kind of day doesn’t come from a flawless centerpiece or perfectly folded napkins. It comes from a plan. “Effortless” doesn’t mean everything is store-bought or the table belongs in a magazine, just that the work is spread across more hands and more days, so Thursday can be about the people.

Consider this your plan: what to decide early, what to make, buy, and delegate, a timeline for two weeks out, two days out, and the day itself, plus the oven, fridge, and cleanup shortcuts that make it all feel easier than it has any right to.

items.title: I Had to Recreate the Olive Oil Sundae From Our Local Pizza Spot
items.standfirst: Our local pizza spot, Paparazzi , is one of those places where it’s all about the ingredients. The sourdough pizza crusts are made fresh daily, there are beautiful Italian…
body: Our local pizza spot, Paparazzi , is one of those places where it’s all about the ingredients. The sourdough pizza crusts are made fresh daily, there are beautiful Italian groceries tucked into the little counter shop, and the soft serve alone is worth a visit.

They have this signature sundae—vanilla soft serve topped with olive oil and pistachios—that might surprise you, until you taste it. One bite and I immediately wanted to make my own version at home. For my spin, I took those same flavors in an affogato-inspired direction: scoops of vanilla ice cream, good olive oil, chopped pistachios, shaved dark chocolate, and flaky salt.

It’s one of my favorite endings for a dinner party , partly because it’s so delicious and partly because there’s no cooking involved. You can set out the toppings and let everyone build their own, which is exactly the level of effort I want to be putting into dessert after making dinner. And it’s always a fun surprise for guests to realize how good olive oil and salt taste on ice cream.
Why Olive Oil and Flaky Salt Belong on Your Desserts
Think about what a little salt does for a chocolate chip cookie , or why salted caramel is so good. That savory edge makes the sweetness more interesting, and olive oil takes it a step further.

Against the cold vanilla ice cream, you really taste the oil’s fruity, slightly peppery flavor. It adds a silky richness, while the pistachios bring crunch and the dark chocolate gives each bite a little bitterness. The flaky salt pulls it all together.

items.title: Pull Out the Good Plates: 9 Dinner Party Table Settings Worth Copying
items.standfirst: Growing up, we gathered with family over dinners served on paper plates with plastic utensils. Parties were casual and relaxed (plus, no one wanted to do the dishes). But on…
body: Growing up, we gathered with family over dinners served on paper plates with plastic utensils. Parties were casual and relaxed (plus, no one wanted to do the dishes). But on holidays, our dinner party table settings were complete with seasonal plates, napkins, and cutlery—and my grandmother always insisted on eating at the formal dining table. It felt special—and it was.

Now, when I host a small group of friends or family, I love to pull out the good plates. I’m one of those old-fashioned gals who actually registered for wedding china, but mine isn’t gathering dust in a cabinet. It’s right there next to our everyday dinner plates. Now, whenever I set the table with those cherished pieces, the whole experience feels elevated—and just as special as my grandma’s table.

That’s still what draws me to a beautifully set table: the feeling that someone has been looking forward to having you over. It might be flowers clipped from the garden, candles lit before the doorbell rings, or a cloth napkin beside a plate of something delicious. The tables I find myself saving have those little signs of care, along with enough room for dinner to happen.

Below, we’ve gathered nine dinner party table setting ideas from real gatherings. There’s a sunlit garden lunch, a table dressed for a celebration, and a candlelit dinner that makes me want to put my phone away. Each offers a different mood for the evening, with ideas you can bring to your own table and the kind of gathering you have in mind.
For a refresher on where the plates, glasses, and flatware go, our guide to setting a table covers the practical details.

items.title: Cooking for Two? These 14 Healthy Dinners Are Portioned Just Right
items.standfirst: Cooking dinner for two should be simple—but somehow, most recipes seem designed to feed a crowd. And while I love having leftovers for lunch the next day, eating the same meal…
body: Cooking dinner for two should be simple—but somehow, most recipes seem designed to feed a crowd. And while I love having leftovers for lunch the next day, eating the same meal all week? Not so much. These healthy dinner recipes for two make it easy to put something nourishing and delicious on the table, with portions that actually make sense for two people.

Whether you’re cooking for your partner, a roommate, or just planning for dinner tonight and lunch tomorrow, this collection includes recipes already portioned for two, plus larger recipes with notes for scaling them down. From quick weeknight meals to dinners worthy of date night, consider this your go-to list for making dinner for two feel effortless.

From veggie-packed dinners to comforting pastas and simple seafood, these are the recipes worth keeping in your weeknight rotation. Whether you have 30 minutes or a little longer, there’s something for every kind of evening.
Burst Tomato, Zucchini, and Burrata Pasta

Jammy tomatoes, golden zucchini, and creamy burrata make this pasta an easy dinner that feels a little special. The original recipe serves four, but you can halve it for two with half the pasta, one zucchini, 1½ cups cherry tomatoes, and 4 ounces of burrata, and half of everything else.

A whole grilled fish makes dinner for two feel like an occasion without an elaborate meal. Finished with a bright, herby salsa verde, this recipe serves two generously and comes together in 30 minutes.

items.title: Skip the 12-Step Routine: A Winter Skincare Plan for Dry, Irritated Skin
items.standfirst: A change of season often brings a change in rhythm. The colder months invite a slower pace: longer nights, warmer, more nourishing meals, and a natural shift in your winter…
body: A change of season often brings a change in rhythm. The colder months invite a slower pace: longer nights, warmer, more nourishing meals, and a natural shift in your winter wellness rituals . But as comforting as this season can feel, winter weather is less kind to your skin. Cold air, low humidity, and indoor heat can lead to dryness, dullness, and irritation, leaving your skin barrier more fragile and in need of extra care. Winter skincare isn’t about taking a more-is-more approach. It’s about intentionally ushering your skin into a season of slowness and comfort.

To help our skin transition to the colder months, I spoke to Malika Sloan, a medical aesthetics expert who gets the VIP clients at her NYC studio, Sloan Studio , ready for seasonal changes. She gave us a full, expert-packed protocol for a winter skincare routine that’s both intentional and effective.
Why your skincare routine needs a winter update

I like to think of the cold-weather switch as a reminder to lean into more thoughtful care. Summer skincare is about whatever feels fastest, easiest, and smoothest under sunscreen . Then comes the cold front. “You have cold air and less humidity outside, then you go inside and the heat is blasting so your skin is constantly being pulled between two very dry environments,” says Sloan.

Harsher weather paired with the stress of the holiday season ( the link between cortisol and skin health may surprise you) can leave skin feeling dry, reactive, and out of balance, making winter a time when our barrier needs a boost.

Dryness. Dryness is often a mix of genetics and environmental stress. Cold temperatures and dry air strip moisture from the skin, leading to flakiness, tightness, and a rough texture. And it’s not just the air outside: Indoor heat contributes to seasonal skin stress, too.

In this episode of Dear Guides, Gabrielle Bernstein shares her five steps to unshakable faith and teaches you how to move from fear and control into trust, grace, and a deeper sense of knowing. body: Ever think you've moved on from someone, only to be reminded of them somehow and get pulled right back into resentment? In this episode of Dear Guides, Gabrielle Bernstein sits down with spiritual intuitive Colette Baron-Reid to explore energetic cords: what they are, how to recognize when you have one, and why rumination is what actually creates and feeds them. Together, they break down the difference between everyday grievances and deeper trauma, why holding onto resentment can block your ability to manifest, and how to release a cord without spiritually bypassing what really happened to you. The episode closes with a guided cord-cutting meditation to help you release resentment, reclaim your energy, and finally let go. Whoever's still living rent-free in your head… let this be the moment you set them free.
